title: There's no such thing as the first banner ad.
description:
There's no such thing as the first banner ad. HotWired launched on 27 October 1994 with 14 advertisers already signed on, and somewhere between six and twelve banner ads went live at the same time that day.

purely to beat a rival to the spot. AT&T had heard that competitor MCI had already secured a HotWired placement and did not want to be left out. The media buy cost roughly $20,000 to $30,000.

Clicking it led to a page of links that had nothing to do with AT&T's products. A clickable map of American art museums, a directory of AT&T websites that existed nowhere else, not even on AT&T's own site, and a short survey.

and even its own retrospective calls it an estimate. The oft-cited 44% click-through rate comes from the ad's creators recalling, decades later, that the rate 'settled at around' that figure once the novelty wore off. Roughly 14 million people were online worldwide at the time.

Only one advertiser out of a dozen that launched that day is remembered as 'the first'.

Sources:
- https://www.fastcompany.com/3037484/the-trailblazing-candy-colored-history-of-the-online-banner-ad: primary 20th-anniversary retrospective interviewing the ad's own creators. Confirms there was no single 'first' banner ad, since 14 advertisers launched with HotWired on 27 October 1994 and somewhere between six and twelve banners appeared simultaneously that day, that AT&T signed on less than a week before launch to compete with rival MCI, paid roughly $20,000 to $30,000 for the placement, that the banner carried no AT&T logo and led to a page of unrelated links, and that the widely cited 44% click-through figure is itself only an approximate, 'by some accounts' recollection.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Will: confirms AT&T's 'You Will' campaign launched in 1993, directed by David Fincher and narrated by Tom Selleck, and that the HotWired banner running from 27 October 1994 reused its tagline.
